# Course description

The course starts with a brief overview of the UAS mapping technology and its rules and regulations. The principles of UAS data collection are explained along with hands-on practice in flight planning and execution. The main focus of this course is on processing the collected imagery using structure from motion technique and deriving orthophoto mosaics and ultra-high resolution digital elevation models of land surface, vegetation and structures. More advanced topics include the fusion of UAS and lidar data, the analysis of multitemporal UAS data, and image classification and change detection with machine learning, with applications in natural resources.

## Prerequisites

 None, but GIS/MEA582 and/or GIS540 or equivalent courses are highly recommended. 

## Recommended reading

There is no required textbook; the course uses online material. These books cover the topics in more depth:

* Frazier, A. E., and Singh, K. K. (eds.), 2021. [Fundamentals of Capturing and Processing Drone Imagery and Data](https://www.routledge.com/Fundamentals-of-Capturing-and-Processing-Drone-Imagery-and-Data/Frazier-Singh/p/book/9781032022499). CRC Press. [NCSU Libraries](https://catalog.lib.ncsu.edu/catalog/NCSU5277219)
* Carrivick, J. L., Smith, M. W., and Quincey, D. J., 2016. [Structure from Motion in the Geosciences](https://www.wiley.com/en-us/Structure+from+Motion+in+the+Geosciences-p-9781118895849). Wiley Blackwell.
* Fahlstrom, P. G., Gleason, T. J., and Sadraey, M. H., 2022. [Introduction to UAV Systems](https://www.wiley.com/en-us/Introduction+to+UAV+Systems%2C+5th+Edition-p-9781119802617), 5th edition. Wiley.
* Barnhart, R. K., Marshall, D. M., and Shappee, E. (eds.), 2021. [Introduction to Unmanned Aircraft Systems](https://www.routledge.com/Introduction-to-Unmanned-Aircraft-Systems/Barnhart-Marshall-Shappee/p/book/9780367366599), 3rd edition. CRC Press. [NCSU Libraries (2nd edition)](https://catalog.lib.ncsu.edu/record/NCSU3721828)
* Jensen, J. R., 2015. Introductory Digital Image Processing: A Remote Sensing Perspective, 4th edition. Pearson.

## Educational Approach

 This course will consist of: lectures, readings, hands-on exercises, homework assignments, and a major project. All the work will be collected within an electronic portfolio that will systematically include the work that you will do for this and other GIS courses. Extra credits will be given for innovative solutions, creativity in problem solving and extensions to given tasks.

## Topics

1. UAS basics: introduction to UAS; rules and regulations for UAS operations
2. Structure from Motion: photogrammetry and SfM concepts; imagery processing in Agisoft Metashape and WebODM
3. UAS flight planning: mission planning and terrain analysis; ground control, checkpoints, and accuracy
4. GIS analytics: analysis of UAS processing results; point cloud analysis
5. Advanced analytics: UAS and lidar data comparison and fusion; analysis of multitemporal UAS data
6. Machine learning and AI: image classification; change detection

## Course Goals
By the end of this course, students will:

Use UAS as a scientific instrument for high-resolution mapping and analysis.
Plan, run, and document a UAS mapping mission while following FAA Part 107 rules.
Process UAS imagery using Agisoft Metashape, WebODM, and GRASS.
Apply UAS-derived data to problems in natural resources, the environment, and the built environment.
Develop reproducible workflows and follow ethical practice in UAS data collection and analysis.

### Course-Level Learning Objectives
By the end of GIS/MEA 584, students will be able to:

* **(Apply)** Plan and run (or simulate) a UAS mapping mission that follows FAA Part 107 and meets stated accuracy requirements.
* **(Apply)** Process raw UAS imagery into georeferenced orthomosaics, digital surface models, and point clouds using Agisoft Metashape, WebODM, and GRASS.
* **(Analyze)** Evaluate UAS-derived products against reference data using positional and surface accuracy metrics.
* **(Evaluate)** Compare UAS Structure from Motion, airborne lidar, and fused datasets, and recommend an appropriate data source for a stated objective.
* **(Create)** Design a complete UAS analysis workflow, from acquisition through interpretation, for a domain-specific problem and present the results in a project portfolio.
